display.title: Episode 223: The Vanishing Bottle of Wine (Pesach)
display.summary_short: A Chol HaMoed Pesach show: 'in every generation' and a skit about a trapped deer, a family visits Studio 604, and a shammes's dream foils a plot to frame the Jews before the king.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Chol HaMoed Pesach, on the eve of the last days of Yom Tov. Uncle Yossi explains the pasuk from the Twelve Pesukim, 'In every generation a person must see himself as if he left Mitzrayim': the miracles and freedom of the Exodus are ours today. A short dramatized skit follows, in which two children dreaming in their pajamas free a deer caught in a bush at 'Mitzvah Stone National Park' and remember how Hashem freed us from Egypt. After the Hakochainik march to 'MiMitzrayim Ge'altanu', a visiting family's children lead the Shema, recite pesukim and say the Rebbe's chapter of Tehillim. The story: a devoted shammes who sleeps above the shul dreams three times of a voice asking, 'Where is the wine for Pesach?' In the Aron HaKodesh he finds the wine bottle replaced with blood, planted by a man named Stepan to accuse the Jews before the king, and swaps it back. On Pesach the king arrives, finds only wine, and Stepan gives himself away. The show ends with the Yom Tov candle-lighting time and news that the contest winners will be announced next week.
display.lesson: Hashem, the Guardian of Israel, never slumbers; in every generation He saves us, and we should feel as if we ourselves left Mitzrayim.

advisories.note: An enemy of the Jews plants a bottle of blood in the shul to accuse them falsely before the king (a blood libel); the plot fails.

privacy.note: A visiting family's children are named in full.

sources_cited.note: 'In every generation a person must see himself as if he left Mitzrayim'; 'had Hashem not taken our fathers out'; 'in every generation they stand against us'.
'The Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.'
The Baal Shem Tov: a Jew is never alone; Hashem is always with him.
